name: Exenatide
summary: A GLP-1 receptor agonist derived from exendin-4, available as a twice-daily injection (Byetta) or once-weekly extended release (Bydureon).
mechanism: Activates the GLP-1 receptor, enhancing glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppressing glucagon, and slowing gastric emptying.
pharmacodynamics: Lowers A1c and weight; the immediate-release form has a particularly strong gastric-emptying (postprandial glucose) effect.

pharmacokinetics.duration: ~6 h per dose (IR twice daily); ER once weekly

dosing.adult: Immediate release: 5 mcg SC twice daily within 60 min before meals, may increase to 10 mcg; ER: 2 mg SC once weekly

contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma
Severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) for the IR formulation
warnings: Acute kidney injury reported with IR form, especially with renal impairment
safety.overdose: Severe nausea, vomiting; supportive care. Hypoglycemia unlikely alone

indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, as add-on therapy
Obesity management in some settings (off-label weight use is common)
clinicalPearls: The twice-daily IR form is dosed before meals, so its postprandial effect is very consistent.
Antibody formation is more common than with other GLP-1s and can blunt response over time.
good: Flexible meal-linked BID dosing or a once-weekly option; weight loss.
bad: Renal impairment (IR), severe GI intolerance, or patients needing a once-daily simple regimen.
